correctness.rationale: Thresholding the attained distances of an injective tuple gives a strict partition chain from the discrete to indiscrete partition, and every such chain defines an ultrametric by first-merge level. dc-homogeneity identifies tuple orbits with these finite order types. Thus injective orbit count is the classical ultradissimilarity/partition-chain number \(a_n\). Allowing repetitions first chooses an equality partition, giving the Stirling transform, and Lengyel's recurrence immediately yields \(b_n=2a_n\). The verifier checks the finite combinatorics.
residual_risks: No correctness defect; rejection is implication/value based.
